class_boundary_assessment: The §4 class boundary as currently sketched (Benten/Willow/IPFS+IPNS-as-mutable IN; TLS/Signal/MLS OUT) is partially right but UNDER-SPECIFIED in three load-bearing ways that L15 attacks at the joint. (a) Filecoin: properly EXCLUDED from Benten's class but for a reason the plan does NOT name — Filecoin signatures authenticate blockchain messages + storage proofs whose validity is gated by the consensus protocol, not by re-verification of historic artifacts by third parties decades later. A 2026 Filecoin storage-proof signature does not need to verify in 2046; by 2046 the deal has expired, the chain has moved on, and what persists is the BLOCKCHAIN STATE (Merkle-committed), not the signature. Filecoin signs the protocol layer, not the persistent-artifact layer. This belongs explicit in §4 — Filecoin is a long-term-persistence system whose signatures are NOT designed to outlive their protocol round, the opposite of Benten Drops. (b) Arweave: properly INCLUDED in Benten's class — Arweave's permaweb explicitly targets ~200-year persistence, signs content with RSA-PSS (classical), has NO public PQ roadmap, and re-validates signatures every time a node serves content. Arweave SHARES Benten's threat model exactly + has not made Benten's choice. The plan must engage with WHY (likely answer: Arweave inherited RSA from its 2018 design lock-in; migrating ~5 PB of signed history to PQ-hybrid is a chain-fork-level event with no clean migration path; the cost-of-incumbent-format-lock is the explanation, NOT a counter-argument to Benten's reasoning). This is actually a STRENGTHENING fact for Benten: 'pick PQ-hybrid before you have a multi-PB legacy you can't migrate' is precisely Benten's pre-v1-freeze argument. (c) git/OpenPGP/Sigstore: misclassified by L15 as 'classical and not moving' — actual ground truth as of 2026-05 is that OpenPGP (the standard substrate for git signing AND a non-trivial fraction of Debian package signing) has draft-ietf-openpgp-pqc at v17 in WG late-stage with composite ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 as MANDATORY, expected H1-2026 RFC publication; Sequoia PGP committed to ship-on-publication; Sigstore (which signs CI artifacts, ML model weights, container images — all 'designed for forever' artifacts) has shipping ML-DSA PoC and Trail-of-Bits-authored architectural agility work explicitly motivated by 'signed today, deployed 20 years' framing. The 'git ships classical' snapshot is true; the 'git's ecosystem is making Benten's choice in parallel' trajectory is also true and must be IN THE BLOG. The honest framing is: Benten is the first SHIPPED P2P content-addressed system to adopt the construction; OpenPGP-WG is independently standardizing the exact same construction (id-MLDSA65-Ed25519-SHA512 / composite ML-DSA-65 + Ed25519) on a parallel timeline; Sigstore architecture is being explicitly retooled for the same threat-model recognition. This is the OPPOSITE of 'alone' and the OPPOSITE of L15's strongest objection. The blog post that engages with this honestly — 'we are early-shipping but well-aligned with an emerging trans-ecosystem consensus that includes OpenPGP and Sigstore' — is rhetorically MUCH STRONGER than the current 'alone' framing.

findings.summary: Sigstore's own PQ-2025 blog explicitly states that PQ-sigs are NOT HNDL-exposed (unlike encrypted content) — this is the same Lens-6 objection but from a system inside Benten's class. The §2.1 framing of 'harvest-now-forge-later' is rhetorically powerful but the symmetry with HNDL-for-encryption is WEAKER than the blog draft implies, because forging a 2026-vintage sig in 2046 requires (a) a CRQC, (b) the public key persisting (which it does in did:key but the SUBSTRATE-DID is replaceable via RotationLog), (c) the adversary planting the forgery into a sync replica where verifiers will encounter it. None of these are equivalent to 'harvested ciphertext is decryptable forever' — the encryption case is structurally simpler + structurally more urgent. The blog should acknowledge this difference rather than claim parallelism.
findings.recommended_change: Add to §2.1 the explicit acknowledgment: 'HNDL-for-signatures is a WEAKER threat than HNDL-for-encryption (which is why X-Wing encryption is unambiguously HNDL-urgent and why we ship it without hesitation). The harvest-now-forge-later threat requires three conditions to coincide — CRQC availability, public-key persistence, and successful injection of forged artifacts into sync replicas — whereas HNDL-for-encryption requires only the first. We argue PQ-hybrid sigs are justified anyway because (a) all three conditions are plausible for Benten's deployment shape, (b) the hybrid construction's marginal cost over classical-only is bounded — the Ed25519 half stays as the audited floor regardless of CRQC timing, (c) deferring the choice means freezing a wire format we cannot evolve post-v1-tag without coordinated migration of all peers. The asymmetry is real but the direction of the argument still holds.' This concession STRENGTHENS the post by pre-empting Lens-6 and L15-class objections.
